title: Would you trust a coding agent to transfer funds if it never had access to your seed phrase?
author: Huge_Woodpecker790
selftext:
I’m looking at connecting a wallet to Claude Code, starting with balance checks and fee estimates. Small transfers would come next, though I’d want to approve them myself until I’d seen how the setup behaves. iron wallet mcp caught my attention because it uses a local signer: the seed stays encrypted on the device, and the agent gets the result of an operation without receiving the seed phrase. It also offers read-only access, limits on individual transactions, and an allowlist for recipients. I haven’t tried it yet, but that gives me a starting point for testing with a separate, low-balance wallet. I’d still be giving the agent access to something that can spend money. It could misread a request and send a payment to an approved recipient, within the allowed amount, without breaking any of those rules. I’d want a confirmation step before signing, at least initially. One thing I’d check early is whether the agent can change its own permissions. If it can add addresses or raise the transfer limit through the same tools it uses to make payments, I’d need to understand what approval those changes require.

The limit itself needs a closer look. Setting a $5 maximum doesn’t tell me whether the agent could make twenty transfers in a row. For anything unattended, I’d want to know whether I can cap the total spend over a session

I’m also curious about failed or delayed responses. After a timeout, the payment may already have gone through; the agent needs a way to check before submitting it again. That’s something I’d test while supervising transfers, with very little money available

If you’re already using an agent for payments, what does it still need your approval for?

comments.author: Automatic_Pea8360
comments.body: Keeping the seed outside the agent is a good starting point. I'd try this with a tiny wallet before involving anything I keep on Ledger. Transfers would still need my approval, especially if the confirmation shows the actual destination and network rather than the agent's summary

comments.author: Only_Asparagus_9937
comments.body: Keeping the seed local is a good starting point. I'd be comfortable testing the setup you described with a tiny balance, but every transfer would still need approval. The confirmation should show the network and recipient, outside the agent's chat

comments.author: Electronic-Amount887
comments.body: The read-only option makes this worth exploring for me. Balance checks and fee estimates are useful without giving anything spending access. Before enabling transfers, I'd want policy changes to require separate approval. A $5 limit means very little if the agent can raise it itself

replies.author: Huge_Woodpecker790
replies.body: That’s where I landed too. I’d keep reads separate from signing, and treat changes to limits or allowlists like a new wallet permission that needs manual approval each time

comments.author: Low_Translator2387
comments.body: The local signer sounds like a sensible design choice. My first test would be the timeout case you mentioned: submit one tiny transfer, interrupt the response, then ask what happened. I'd want a persistent operation id that survives a client restart, with status checked before another submission. Having transaction history available helps, but I'd still approve retries until that behavior is clear

comments.author: Mobile-Growth2053
comments.body: For a separate spending wallet, this sounds pretty reasonable. I like being able to start read-only in the same client instead of building a signing setup myself. I'd keep savings on a Ledger, though. Unattended payments would need a total budget enforced outside the agent, including fees, before I'd consider enabling them

replies.author: Huge_Woodpecker790
replies.body: Keeping savings separate is the line I’d draw too. The fee point is easy to miss - a session cap that excludes fees can overshoot faster than expected when the network gets busy

comments.author: Huge_Woodpecker790
comments.body: That independent confirmation screen is the part I care about most too. It needs to show the exact recipient, network, amount, and fee so the chat can't quietly reinterpret what I meant

comments.author: ApartmentOk3498
comments.body: keep every transfer behind a manual confirm
